- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag filter to smooth out overshoots.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days), model often misses mean reversion; anchor forecast to 30-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply a downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per sentiment drop >0.3.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to underestimate price peaks; add 0.5–1.0% buffer if sentiment remains positive or shows momentum.
